atoms.name: Alpha Node
atoms.description: The present-observer surface mark — Peat's live current primary location on Earth, the single movable node among six fixed archive marks.
atoms.rationale: SBA-1 visual.md §2.4 / spec §5.1 (enriched 2026-05-29) — α is Peat's live current primary location ('ที่อยู่หลัก ณ เวลานั้น'): movable, self-updated by Peat, NETRA-tracked because Peat tells NETRA where he is. When Peat travels, α relocates (Bangkok at home, Tokyo/Kyoto in Japan, etc.). The six archive nodes (003 Kyoto · 002 Chiang Mai · 001 Yirgacheffe · 000 SF · 012 Tokyo · 047 Point Nemo) are fixed GPS coordinates of past record-making — 'where it was recorded.' α = 'here, now.' Archive nodes = 'where it was surveyed.' They may overlap (e.g. α at Tokyo over 012) — present-observer-over-past-archive layering, intended. Visual encoding: α is the only orange node (var(--accent-orange), 0.022 radius, pulsing ring halo); archive nodes are teal var(--ink-primary), 0.012 radius, quiet. Orange = live observer; teal = archive. SBA-1 §summary statement 4.

variants.name: default
variants.description: Resting present-observer mark — accent-orange dot with a soft accent-orange-soft halo ring on paper. The single orange node among six teal archive marks.

variants.name: active
variants.description: Reticle-anchored state — same dot, intensified accent-orange ring, used when the camera or NETRA reticle is locked onto alpha.

variants.name: selected
variants.description: Coord-pin open — the alpha dot with its halo plus an outer reticle ring while the alpha coord-pin (place / coords / why: present observer) reads. NOTE: alpha has NO 'dimmed' state — per attractor-binding §6.4 the observer locus is excluded from attractor dimming; the orange ring is the observer marker, not an attractor halo, so alpha never quiets to 0.32 opacity when an attractor is active. This is a documented exclusion, not a missing state.

atoms.name: HUD Corner Readout
atoms.description: Instrument readings pinned to the four corners of the globe canvas — OBSERVING / CAMERA / alpha / SCALE.
atoms.rationale: SBA-1 visual.md §1.6 / spec §8.4 — the four globe-canvas corners carry live instrument readings in mono 7px 0.22em, ink-soft with bold promoted to ink-primary. SBA-1 §summary statement 5 (mono uppercase as instrument register).
atoms.single_variant_rationale: INTENTIONALLY SINGLE-VARIANT. The HUD readout text changes with cameraFocus (ORBIT·0° shifts to the current angle; OBSERVING mode may update), but the CSS rule set does not change — this is content state, not visual-atom state. Variants express visual STATES or FIDELITY LEVELS, not content updates (per MANIFEST-SCHEMA.md 'Variants discipline'). The four-corner layout, the ink-soft/ink-primary token pair, and the mono type scale are invariant across all camera states. Parity note: netra-voice-strip (A06) carries rest/attractor variants because its SURFACE TOKEN changes (voice strip background); the HUD corners do not change their surface tokens. Single-variant is correct here, not a gap.

atoms.name: Globe
atoms.description: The A.T.L.A.S. paper-instrument globe — aged paper sphere with lat/lon contours inside a dashed cartographic frame; full Three.js fidelity, with a standby fallback at narrow viewports.
atoms.rationale: SBA-1 visual.md §2.1-2.3 / §summary statements 1-3 — a paper instrument that contains a surveyed archive (the frame commands, the globe is evidence inside it); aged seeded paper grain with lat/lon contours; three co-equal spatial systems (surface / axis / orbit) visible through each other via transparency. The standby variant preserves the garden-under-survey feeling when Three.js retires (SBA-1 §3 D5 / §4 F6).

variants.name: full
variants.description: Faithful Three.js render (>=601px) — the SAME scene production ships: MeshStandard paper-cream sphere with a real Earth coastline silhouette multiplied through it (earth_specular_2048.jpg, 0.28 / blur 1.2px), 7 irregular contour rings, 3 NeX wireframe shells (1.18/1.32/1.48x) + 48 Fibonacci radial rays, the dashed-orange worldline arc, the inner shade sphere, the Ne0N axis spine through the poles with survey-triangle caps + orange pole beacons, the alpha observer node at Bangkok GPS (0.022 radius orange sphere + RingGeometry 0.034–0.044 halo), and 6 teal archive nodes at real GPS (003 Kyoto / 002 Chiang Mai / 001 Yirgacheffe / 000 SF / 012 Tokyo / 047 Point Nemo; 0.012 radius teal var(--ink-primary) spheres, no halo). Node system per spec §5.2–5.3 (TASK-2026-05-29-SOUL-FACTORY-GLOBE-NODES, Sirius 2026-05-29): alpha = live observer orange only; archive = teal fixed marks. Mounted on the .atlas-globe-wrap cartographic frame via a local r160 three.module.js (vendored beside this manifest; no CDN for the library, no build step). Ported from the locked v1 prototype and reconciled against the living baseline components/WorldlineGlobe.tsx (production wins on divergence).

variants.name: standby
variants.description: Miniaturised LIVE globe — the SAME live Three.js instrument as the full render, shrunk to a portable 140px unit (140px MID / 120px NARROW per Betelgeuse's reconciled spec §11 L344; TASK-2026-05-29-SOUL-FACTORY-MINI-LIVE, Peat's จัดเต็ม directive). This OVERRIDES spec §11's prior 'Three.js retires <=600px' rule (Betelgeuse reconciling §11 in parallel). Mounts a real Three.js earth-coastline sphere (lower-resolution texture 512x256 + capped devicePixelRatio 1.5) with the Ne0N axis spine through the poles + orange pole beacons, the alpha observer node at Bangkok GPS (orange sphere + ring halo), and one faint NeX wireframe shell hint — gentle auto-rotate. The heaviest full-render layers (48-ray Fibonacci field, 3-shell stack, 7 contour rings, worldline arc, ordinary archive nodes) are dropped/scaled for portability so it is cheap to instantiate. Reads as the SAME soul at fidelity loss, not a different object. DEGRADATION: the live mini uses ESM Three.js, so on file:// / no-WebGL / prefers-reduced-motion the static 2D paper-canvas mini (130x130 radial-gradient body + lat/lon repeating-linear grid + orange alpha dot with 5px halo per spec §11) shows instead — same file:// fallback pattern as the full panel. All colour tokenised; runtime canvas geometry is documented-exempt (gate-exempt module script) and cited to spec §11 L327.

atoms.name: Archive Node
atoms.description: The teal Ne0 surface mark — a fixed past archive entry surveyed at real GPS. 'Where it was recorded.'
atoms.rationale: SBA-1 §2.4 / §summary 4 / spec §5.2-5.3 — surveyed nodes at real GPS with narrative reasons; not data points, surveyed marks. The archive node is the fixed-past counterpart to the movable alpha observer: var(--ink-primary) teal, 0.012 radius sphere, no halo, quiet. Six exist today (003 Kyoto / 002 Chiang Mai / 001 Yirgacheffe / 000 SF / 012 Tokyo / 047 Point Nemo). Teal = archive; orange = live observer. Cataloged here as a first-class node type so the master design is complete on node TYPES (alpha-node A03 already exists as the orange observer; archive is its teal sibling), not only a sub-pixel dot inside the globe (A12). The CSS render in the gallery is a colour/concept guide only — canonical render is the Three.js SphereGeometry(0.012) in nodeMatInk teal.

atoms.description: The orange-stroked square — the reserved Ne0 glyph for photo entries. Future; not yet a live glyph.
atoms.rationale: RESERVED — spec §15 item 1 / attractor-binding §2.2 (future). When photo entries ship, their surface marks become orange-stroked squares instead of circles so the eye reads 'image, not article' at a glance; the membership halo follows the square silhouette. The square + orange stroke are the reserved vocabulary — cataloged here so the master design is COMPLETE on node TYPES and the MIRAI phase builds on a known foundation, but NO production glyph exists yet (the surface pin loop in components/WorldlineGlobe.tsx renders only teal circles today). The state set (default/hover/selected/dimmed) will mirror archive-node with a square halo, but is DEFERRED to the photo-entry phase and is intentionally not specified now — this atom marks the type as first-class without prematurely designing its states. Do not implement until the photo-entry surface is dispatched (spec §15 → TASK-33).

atoms.name: Focus Button (Camera-Aid)
atoms.description: The stratum navigation / camera-focus control present on every globe surface — ink-bordered button with glyph, label-id, label-role, and a key badge; three visual states.
atoms.rationale: SBA-1 visual.md §1.7 / spec §8.1 — the strata sidebar lists every Ne0/Ne1/NeX layer as a distinct camera-focus target; the button row is the primary interaction surface for redirecting the globe camera. Like the attractor-pill, the focus button is a first-class control atom: it has a default state, an interactive hover state, and a selection state (is-active when the camera is locked to this stratum). SBA-1 §summary statement 5 (mono uppercase instrument register) — the label-id and label-role follow the mono 10px / 7.5px scale; the key badge is Special Elite. Source: globals.css .atlas-strata-btn (L471–522), present on every globe surface load. Cataloged here because it was missing from the master as a named atom (G3 gap from whole-gallery audit, TASK-2026-05-29-SOUL-FACTORY-NODE-FAMILY §4); the attractor-pill (A10) establishes the control-atom cataloguing pattern.
